    The link [Retirer] is generated by lines 4–6. When the link is clicked, the method [Form].retirerPersonne will be executed. It’s time to examine the [Form.java] class:

    
package forms;
 
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import javax.enterprise.context.RequestScoped;
import javax.faces.bean.ManagedBean;
import javax.faces.bean.SessionScoped;
 
@ManagedBean
@SessionScoped
public class Form {
 
  // model
  private List<Personne> personnes;
  private int personneId;
 
  // manufacturer
  public Form() {
    // initialization of the list of persons
    personnes = new ArrayList<Personne>();
    personnes.add(new Personne(1, "dupont", "jacques"));
    personnes.add(new Personne(2, "durand", "élise"));
    personnes.add(new Personne(3, "martin", "jacqueline"));
  }
 
  public String retirerPersonne() {
    // search for the selected person
    int i = 0;
    for (Personne personne : personnes) {
      // current person = selected person?
      if (personne.getId() == personneId) {
        // delete the current person from the list
        personnes.remove(i);
        // we're done
        break;
      } else {
        // next person
        i++;
      }
    }
    // we test on the same page
    return null;
  }
  
  // getters and setters
...
}
    • lines 18–24: the constructor initializes the list of people from line 14,
    • Line 10: Because this list must persist across requests, the bean's scope is the session.

    When the [retirerPersonne] method on line 26 is executed, the field on line 15 has been initialized by the id of the person whose [Retirer] link was clicked:

    
          <h:commandLink value="Retirer" action="#{form.retirerPersonne}">
            <f:setPropertyActionListener target="#{form.personneId}" value="#{personne.id}"/>
</h:commandLink>

    The <f:setPropertyActionListener> tag allows information to be transferred to the model. Here, the value of the value attribute is copied into the model field identified by the target attribute. Thus, the id of the current person—the one to be removed from the list of people—is copied into the [Form].personneId field via that field’s getter. This is done before the method referenced by the action attribute in line 1 is executed.

    Lines 26–43: The method [supprimerPersonne] removes the person whose id is equal to personneId.

    2.11. Example mv-jsf2-09: Layout of a JSF application

    2.11.1. The application

    The application demonstrates how to layout a JSF application with two views:

    The application has two views:

    • in [1], page 1,
    • in [2], page 2.

    You can navigate between the two pages. What we want to show here is that pages 1 and 2 share a common layout, as shown in the screenshots above.

    The application’s Netbeans project is as follows:

    2.11.4. The page [page1.xhtml]

    The page [layout.xhtml] is not intended to be viewed. It serves as a template for the pages [page1.xhtml] and [page2.xhtml]. This is referred to as a page template. The page [page1.xhtml] is as follows:

    
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' ?>
<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd">
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
      xmlns:h="http://java.sun.com/jsf/html"
      xmlns:f="http://java.sun.com/jsf/core"
      xmlns:ui="http://java.sun.com/jsf/facelets">
  <ui:composition template="layout.xhtml">
    <ui:define name="contenu">
      <h2>page 1</h2>
      <h:commandLink value="page 2" action="page2"/>
    </ui:define>
  </ui:composition>
</html>
    • line 6, the namespace ui is used;
    • line 7, we specify that the page is associated with the [layout.xhtml] template using a <ui:composition> tag,
    • line 8: this association ensures that each <ui:define> tag will be associated with a <ui:insert> tag from the template being used, in this case [layout.xhtml]. The link is established via the name attribute of both tags. They must be identical.

    The displayed page is [layout.xhtml], where the content of each <ui:insert> tag is replaced by the content of the <ui:define> tag from the requested page. Here, it is as if the displayed page were:

    
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' ?>
<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd">
 
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
      xmlns:h="http://java.sun.com/jsf/html"
      xmlns:f="http://java.sun.com/jsf/core"
      xmlns:ui="http://java.sun.com/jsf/facelets">
  <h:head>
    <title>JSF</title>
    <h:outputStylesheet library="css" name="styles.css"/>
  </h:head>
  <h:body style="background-image: url('${request.contextPath}/resources/images/standard.jpg');">
    <h:form id="formulaire">
      <table style="width: 400px">
        <tr>
          <td colspan="2" bgcolor="#ccccff">
            <ui:include src="entete.xhtml"/>
          </td>
        </tr>
        <tr style="height: 200px">
          <td bgcolor="#ffcccc">
            <ui:include src="menu.xhtml"/>
          </td>
          <td>
              <h2>page 1</h2>
              <h:commandLink value="page 2" action="page2"/>
          </td>
        </tr>
        <tr bgcolor="#ffcc66">
          <td colspan="2">
            <ui:include src="basdepage.xhtml"/>
          </td>
        </tr>         
      </table>
    </h:form>
  </h:body>
</html>

    Lines 25–26 of [page1.xhtml] were inserted in place of the <ui:insert> tag from [layout.xml].

    The page [page2.xhtml] is similar to [page1.xhtml]:

    
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' ?>
<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd">
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
      xmlns:h="http://java.sun.com/jsf/html"
      xmlns:f="http://java.sun.com/jsf/core"
      xmlns:ui="http://java.sun.com/jsf/facelets">
  <ui:composition template="layout.xhtml">
    <ui:define name="contenu">
      <h2>page 2</h2>
      <h:commandLink value="page 1" action="page1"/>
    </ui:define>
  </ui:composition>
</html>

    2.12. Conclusion

    The study just conducted on JSF 2 is far from exhaustive. However, it is sufficient to understand the examples that follow. For further details, refer to [ref2].

    2.13. Testing with Eclipse

    Let’s show how to test Maven projects with the SpringSource Tool Suite:

    • In [1], import a Maven project [2], which you select using the [3] button. Here, we use the Maven project [mv-jsf2-09] for Eclipse
    • in [4], the imported project has been correctly recognized as a Maven project [5],
    • in [6], the project imported into the project explorer,
    • in [7], it is running on a Tomcat server [8],
    • in [10], Tomcat 7 was launched,
    • in [11], the [mv-jsf2-09] [11] project home page is displayed in a browser within Eclipse.
